name: Dollymount Strand
notes: Designated set-up/launch/land area at the wooden bridge end; stay 200 m from swimmers. Flat at low tide, best in southerlies. Alternatives: Poolbeg / Shelly Banks (flat ~4 h around high tide), Sutton – Burrow Beach (N–NE), Portmarnock (SE or N–NE), Rush South Beach (waves in S–SW).

name: Lady's Island Lake
notes: Brackish lagoon, standing depth, butter flat; best in southerlies. Keep away from the tern islands and the northern reserve (summer breeding). Alternative: Rosslare Strand (S–SE, groynes every ~300 m).

name: Tramore
notes: Open beach for all levels; lagoon behind the dunes at high tide. Surfers at the town end.

name: Garrylucas
notes: Cork's main kite beach (Garrettstown/Garrylucas), kite school; kickers in swell. SW best.

name: Inch Beach
notes: Wide sandy beach, flat to freeride.

name: Brandon Bay (Castlegregory)
notes: 17 km bay from Fermoyle to the Maharees: world-class waves in W–NW; gusty near the mountains. Experienced riders.

name: Maharees – Sandy Bay
notes: Tralee Bay side of the Castlegregory isthmus: sheltered flat water, Jamie Knox watersports centre.

name: Lahinch
notes: Popular surf town: waves, experienced riders; W–SW cross-shore. Keep clear of surfers.

name: Galway – Silverstrand (Barna)
notes: Main Galway lesson spot; shallow flat lagoon at low tide. SW–W winds. Rusheen Bay next door is flat and sheltered.

name: Achill – Keel
notes: Keel Strand for waves (gusty in NW), Keel Lough 100 m inland: knee-deep flat water, kite school, Battle of the Lake event.

name: Enniscrone
notes: Wide sandy bay, flat water, popular with kiters.

name: Rossnowlagh
notes: Versatile, kite school; narrow at high tide. Alternative: Bundoran – Tullan Strand (army range: obey red flags).

name: Dunfanaghy – Killahoey
notes: Open beach plus the flat Dunfanaghy lagoon behind it. Alternative: Downings (Sheephaven Bay, sheltered; Carrigart lagoon).
